42. Trapping Rain Water

Difficulty: Hard | Acceptance: 62.4%

Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Example 1:

Input: height = [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1] Output: 6 Explanation: The above elevation map (black section) is represented by array [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]. In this case, 6 units of rain water (blue section) are trapped.

Example 2:

Input: height = [4,2,0,3,2,5] Output: 9

Constraints:

  • n == height.length
  • 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 10^5
